answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because lagoon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, basalt is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any ocean approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
